findings.title: Sync pull loop against an unreachable/revoked hub: no exponential backoff in the sync use-cases (observed storm in the Oct-10 live log)
findings.evidence: 2026-10-10 live log (erp.1.log, 8.3MB): POST /api/sync/run every ~15-20s (5347 calls/day) while the hub answered 403 SYNC_DEVICE_REVOKED and undici timeouts — the loop kept polling a revoked/unreachable hub. Commit 15c66ab7 ('A successful pull clears the hub-unreachable mark') shows hub-unreachable state tracking exists; whether a REVOKED/403 state STOPS the loop (vs. just marking it) was not verified line-by-line in the frontend hook within this session's budget.
findings.expected_behavior: A revoked/unreachable hub backs off exponentially and surfaces a clear UI state instead of polling every ~15s indefinitely.
findings.actual_behavior: Observed: continuous ~15-20s polling with 403s (Oct-10 log). The unreachable MARK exists; the backoff/stop behavior on REVOKED is unverified.
findings.root_cause: Not established — either the hook lacks backoff on terminal states, or the Oct-09 build predates the fix.
findings.reproduction_steps: Revoke the device hub-side (or cut the hub), watch POST /api/sync/run cadence in logs over 10 minutes.
findings.potential_impact: Battery/network waste; log noise; a permanently revoked device never gives up. No data-integrity impact (idempotent, ordered).
findings.related_tests: verify-sync-multidevice.mjs (advisory CI, 17-27/33 non-deterministic per its own comment)
findings.missing_tests: No test for the revoked-hub backoff/stop behavior.
findings.recommended_fix: Verify useAutoSync's handling of SYNC_DEVICE_REVOKED/hub-unreachable; if it keeps polling, stop the loop on terminal 403 and show 'الجهاز مُبطَل من المركز' in the sync screen.

findings.title: Multi-device convergence drill is non-deterministic (17-27 of 33 on identical code) and runs advisory in CI
findings.evidence: ci.yml comment: 'the multi-device drill reuses a template database and leaks state between scenarios, so its score varies run to run (observed 17–27 of 33 on identical code). Making a non-deterministic script a hard gate would fail honest PRs at random... promote it to a blocking gate once the template is rebuilt per run.' It is continue-on-error today.
findings.expected_behavior: A deterministic convergence proof that can gate releases.
findings.actual_behavior: Advisory only, with known state leakage between scenarios.
findings.root_cause: Template DB reuse across scenarios; documented as a known limitation with a planned fix.
findings.reproduction_steps: cd backend && node scripts/verify-sync-multidevice.mjs twice on identical code; compare scores.
findings.potential_impact: Sync convergence regressions can escape CI (the drill is advisory); the unit/integration suites cover the pieces but not the end-to-end two-device drill deterministically.
findings.missing_tests: Deterministic per-run template rebuild for the drill.
findings.recommended_fix: Rebuild the template per run (the CI comment's own plan) and promote to a blocking gate.

findings.title: prettier --check . fails on 100 files (92 source) and no CI gate prevents it
findings.evidence: npx prettier --check . -> exit 1, 100 files (92 source + 8 docs). ci.yml contains NO prettier --check step. Root eslint ignores backend/** (M-09); backend eslint is the pg-import boundary only (D-006) — so neither lint config covers the drifted files. The failing source files are exactly those from the recent sync commits (2b9b602c/5ee79610/7eaabec1): backend/src/infrastructure/orm/**, backup/sqliteBackup.ts, schema-fingerprint.json.
findings.expected_behavior: Formatting is enforced somewhere so new code cannot land unformatted.
findings.actual_behavior: No enforcement: CI has no prettier step; both eslint configs exclude the drifted files; the repo's own npm run format (prettier --write .) is manual.
findings.root_cause: The SQLite-engine/backup work was synced via 'full working tree' commits without running the formatter; the gate that would have caught it doesn't exist in CI.
findings.reproduction_steps: npx prettier --check . (exit 1, 100 files); grep prettier .github/workflows/ci.yml (no match).
findings.potential_impact: Formatting drift in the newest engine code; 'npm run format' would rewrite 100 files in one commit — a large, review-hostile diff. No functional impact (typecheck+tests pass).
findings.recommended_fix: Add a prettier --check step to CI (scoped to exclude the audit .md reports, or add them to .prettierignore) and format the drifted files in a dedicated commit.
findings.regression_risks: Low (formatting only); the diff will be large — do it as its own commit.

findings.title: 46 SQLite twins drifted from their PostgreSQL sources — behavioral parity is tool-unverifiable for them
findings.evidence: node backend/scripts/port-sqlite-repos.mjs --check -> 46 'drift:' lines (PG source changed; twin stamp stale). Includes SqliteInvoiceRepository, SqlitePartyRepository, SqliteCashboxRepository, SqliteLedgerRepository, SqliteDashboardRepository, partyDeletionImpact.ts, keysetPage.ts, documentNumbers.ts, dayLockHelper.ts, rollLocking.ts, rollDeletionHelper.ts, inventoryCountRepository.ts, financialYearRepository.ts, dyePurgeRepository.ts, customerCredit.ts, cashboxBalanceHelper.ts, partyListStatsAggregation.ts, reportAggregates.ts + more.
findings.expected_behavior: Each twin carries a PORTED-FROM sha256 matching its PG source so drift is detectable.
findings.actual_behavior: 46 twins' stamps no longer match; whether their BEHAVIOR still matches requires manual review (documented as known in CLAUDE.md — 'don't re-stamp without reviewing').
findings.root_cause: PG-side fixes (the 31-finding remediation, Oct 11) were applied without re-stamping every twin; the check is advisory, not a CI gate.
affected_endpoints: all endpoints whose repository has a twin
affected_workflows: every business workflow on the desktop engine
findings.potential_impact: A PG fix may be missing (or divergent) in the desktop engine — the two engines can behave differently on the same input. UNVERIFIED which of the 46 have real behavioral divergence (stamp staleness ≠ behavior divergence — e.g. comment-only changes also stale the stamp).
findings.related_tests: backend suite runs on BOTH engines (the SQLite run passed 958/958) — this is the real parity safety net, and it is green.
findings.missing_tests: No per-twin behavioral diff; the stamp check is not a CI gate.
findings.recommended_fix: Make port-sqlite-repos --check a CI gate (advisory->blocking once the 46 are reviewed), and review each drifted twin for real behavioral divergence (prioritize invoice/party/cashbox/ledger/deletion-impact).
findings.regression_risks: Re-stamping without review would HIDE real divergence — the current advisory state is the safer default.

findings.title: SQLite journal pgReference bookkeeping stale: 0005_drive_archive records pgRef 101 while its content mirrors PG journal 102
findings.evidence: sqlite journal: 0005_drive_archive -> pgRef 101; PG journal max idx = 102 (20261025_settings_drive_section). 0005_drive_archive.sql:80-84 contains '-- PG 20261025_settings_drive_section ...' + ALTER TABLE "settings" ADD COLUMN "drive" — i.e. the migration CONTENT mirrors PG 102 while its bookkeeping says 101.
findings.expected_behavior: pgReferenceJournalIdx reflects the highest PG journal index mirrored by the SQLite migration (102).
findings.actual_behavior: pgReferenceJournalIdx = 101 although the file mirrors PG 102.
findings.root_cause: The combined 0005 migration (motard_drive_* runtime tables + the settings.drive mirror) was added without bumping the pgReference field.
findings.reproduction_steps: Compare max(pgReferenceJournalIdx) in sqlite/migrations/meta/_journal.json (101) with PG journal max idx (102); then read 0005_drive_archive.sql lines 80-84.
findings.potential_impact: Any automated drift check comparing 'last SQLite pgRef vs PG max idx' reports a FALSE drift — it misled this audit's DB subagent and this auditor's first pass (both nearly filed a phantom 'missing settings.drive migration' defect). No runtime impact; the schema is correct.
findings.related_tests: tests/desktop-pending-migrations.test.ts (checks pending migrations, not pgRef bookkeeping)
findings.missing_tests: No test asserts pgReferenceJournalIdx equals the highest mirrored PG index.
findings.recommended_fix: Bump 0005_drive_archive pgReferenceJournalIdx to 102 (content already matches), or add a comment documenting the intentional 101.

findings.title: Desktop migration tracking has two tables; the drizzle schema_migrations table is dead
findings.evidence: Live desktop DB (read-only copy of %LOCALAPPDATA%\motard-erp\data\motard.db) has an EMPTY schema_migrations table (columns version/applied_at/applied_by/description/checksum/success; rows: []). The desktop runtime applies migrations from the journal and records progress in motard_meta.schema_journal_idx (runtime.ts:153,163,204).
findings.expected_behavior: One source of truth for applied migrations.
findings.actual_behavior: Two tracking mechanisms; the drizzle schema_migrations table is never written by the desktop runner.
findings.root_cause: The SQLite baseline carries drizzle's bookkeeping table, but the desktop runtime uses its own journal+meta approach.
findings.reproduction_steps: SELECT * FROM schema_migrations on any live desktop DB -> 0 rows; read runtime.ts applyMigration/motard_meta flow.
findings.potential_impact: Misleading for operators/support querying 'which migrations ran'; no functional impact.
findings.recommended_fix: Document that motard_meta.schema_journal_idx is the desktop source of truth; optionally drop the unused table from the baseline in a future regeneration.

findings.title: settings.drive column exists in the live desktop DB? NO — explained by the stale Oct 9 build, not a missing migration
findings.symbol: ALTER TABLE settings ADD COLUMN drive
findings.evidence: Live motard.db settings columns: [id, tenant_id, company, currencies, payment_methods, taxes, units, warehouses, printing, updated_at] — NO drive; SELECT drive -> 'no such column: drive'. BUT 0005_drive_archive.sql:84 DOES add it, and the SS-01 allowlist test (tests/sqlite/settings-section-allowlist.test.ts) PASSES 4/4 on a fresh SQLite DB built by the real runtime (I ran: DB_ENGINE=sqlite npx vitest run tests/sqlite/settings-section-allowlist.test.ts -> 4 passed, incl. upsertSection('drive', {})). The live DB was created by the shipped 2.0.4 build (Oct 9 20:50), which predates commit 2b9b602c (Oct 11) that introduced 0005 + the schema column.
findings.expected_behavior: A DB built by current code has settings.drive.
findings.actual_behavior: The live (old-build) DB lacks it; a fresh DB from current code has it (proven by the passing test).
findings.root_cause: Not a migration gap — the shipped installer lags HEAD (see F-NEW-01). First audit pass almost filed this as Critical; the live-DB check + the SS-01 test run corrected it.
findings.reproduction_steps: n/a — negative result documented to prevent a future false finding.
findings.potential_impact: None once the app is rebuilt from current HEAD. (With the stale build, a settings read after upgrading code-in-place would fail with 'no such column: drive' — the desktop must be REBUILT, not just the code updated.)
findings.recommended_fix: No code fix. Rebuild the desktop installer from HEAD (ties to F-NEW-01).

findings.title: Rate limiting exists only on the auth routes; financial POSTs have none
findings.evidence: grep -rln 'rateLimit|express-rate-limit' backend/src/presentation/routes/ -> only auth.route.ts. All other routes (invoice, voucher, cashbox, expense, ledger, party, return, order, print, roll, statement) enforce idempotency-key instead (13 route files, required:true on financial POSTs).
findings.expected_behavior: Brute-force protection on credential endpoints; authenticated financial endpoints protected by auth + idempotency.
findings.actual_behavior: Exactly that. No rate limit on authenticated financial POSTs.
findings.root_cause: Design choice: the abuse vector for financial endpoints is an authenticated session; unauthenticated flooding is blocked at the auth gate which IS rate-limited.
findings.reproduction_steps: grep the routes dir for rate-limit imports; observe only auth.route.ts matches.
findings.potential_impact: An authenticated insider can fire unlimited requests; bounded by UI usage patterns. No unauthenticated exposure.
findings.missing_tests: No load/abuse test on authenticated endpoints.
findings.recommended_fix: Optional: add a per-user rate limit on financial POSTs if abuse becomes a concern.

findings.title: server-bundle.test.mjs cannot run in this environment (port 8080 occupied)

findings.actual_behavior: Blocked by an unrelated listener; the other 9 desktop gates pass 24/24.

findings.potential_impact: One packaging gate unverified in THIS environment; it passes in CI (fresh runners).
findings.recommended_fix: Re-run when 8080 is free (or on CI).
